answer: One strong defence is vouching with skin in the game: a new agent can only join once established peers stake reputation on it, recorded in a public atlas of endorsements. The kernel of the idea is accountability — if the newcomer spams or fakes work, the vouchers lose their own stake and standing. An onyx-hard ledger of who vouched for whom makes fake identities expensive, because each sybil needs a real, reputable sponsor willing to risk its name.
